title: Determination of the Magnetic Penetration Depth from Finite-Element Susceptibility Calculations of Spheroidal and Cylindrical Superconductors
abstract: The magnetic penetration depth, $λ$, is a fundamental parameter of the superconducting state and is commonly determined from precision measurements of the magnetic susceptibility, $χ$, in the Meissner state. However, extracting $λ$ from such measurements requires an accurate treatment of geometry-dependent demagnetization effects, for which analytic results are only available in a limited number of cases. Here we present a finite-element analysis of the magnetic response of three dimensional superconducting spheroids and cylinders with finite penetration depth. By calculating the magnetic moment and susceptibility, $χ(λ)$, over a wide range of aspect ratios, we quantify the shape-dependent Meissner response and extract effective demagnetization factors in the $λ\rightarrow 0$ limit. For small but finite $λ$, we further determine effective sample dimensions from the initial variation of $χ(λ)$ and propose an improved analytical expression for these. Our results provide a high-precision procedure for determining $λ$ from volume-exclusion based susceptibility measurements and should be directly applicable to the characterization of novel superconducting materials.
summary: This work develops a high-precision, finite-element simulation technique to calculate the magnetic susceptibility of superconducting spheroids and cylinders. By accurately modeling geometry-dependent demagnetization effects, the authors provide reliable methods to extract the fundamental magnetic penetration depth ($\lambda$) from susceptibility measurements. This is crucial for characterizing novel superconducting materials using volume-exclusion techniques.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately determining the magnetic penetration depth ($\lambda$) of superconductors from magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$) measurements, which is complicated by geometry-dependent demagnetization effects.
main_result: The authors provide a high-precision, finite-element analysis procedure to quantify the shape-dependent Meissner response and derive improved analytical expressions for effective demagnetization factors and sample dimensions.
method: The primary method involves solving the London equation using finite-element analysis (FEA) in three dimensions for superconducting spheroids and cylinders.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a superconductor (spheroids and cylinders) characterized by a finite magnetic penetration depth ($\lambda$). The physics is governed by the London equation and the resulting magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$).
key_observables: Magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$), effective demagnetization factor ($N$), effective dimension ($R$), and the magnetic moment per unit field ($m/H$).
important_parameters:
Penetration depth ($\lambda$), aspect ratio ($
u = c/a$), and the ratio $\lambda/a$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes axial symmetry for computational efficiency and relies on linear approximations for small changes in $\lambda$ when relating measurements to $\Delta\lambda$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometry of the modeled superconductors (spheroids/cylinders) and show calculated field profiles ($H/H_0$) and radial field distributions for varying $\lambda/a$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem, details the FEA methodology for calculating $\chi(\lambda)$, presents results for demagnetization factors and effective dimensions by comparing numerical findings to known analytical solutions, and concludes with guidelines for experimental application.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter electromagnetism, the rigorous numerical treatment of boundary conditions and the development of generalized fitting functions for geometric parameters (like $R$) showcase advanced computational physics techniques applicable to complex quantum systems.
